title: Branches from the public home reach integration as merge requests
goal: kbgit.py bridge <branch> fetches the branch from the publish remote, takes its commits not on the publish remote's main, refuses (exit 1) when one touches kb/_querylog, rebases them onto the integration main (a conflict exits 3 with the rebase left in progress, as sync), runs the gate and sends them through sync's lane routing (content to main, code as code/<id>); it never writes to the publish remote; tests.py -k TestBridge covers a content branch, a code branch and a conflict with local bare remotes

gates.question: bridge rebases a public pull request's commits onto the integration main, so their hashes change and the public home never marks the pull request merged by itself. What happens to the pull request?
options: bridge prints the pull request's branch and the integration commits; a person closes it once publish brings them
bridge closes it with gh pr close and a comment naming the integration commits, once they are on the integration main
pull requests are not accepted: the public home is read-only for contributors
gates.recommendation: bridge prints the pull request's branch and the integration commits; a person closes it once publish brings them

notes: Cloud sessions clone from GitHub and push only their working branch (QK-plugin-host-cloud-session-push-automatic). Mirroring never brings pull requests and pull mirroring is Premium (repository-mirroring.md:18, :36); on Free a Git client fetch and push is the path (:39), which bridge is. git.md already says branches from the public home reach the integration remote by a rebase, never a merge of the two histories. The rebase changes the commits' hashes, so the public home does not see its pull request's commits reach main (detecting-mr-merges-in-ci.md:31 needs the same commits).
